text:
lia: quick heads-up 11 opened a tiny PR to fix the embeddings reference. the request example shows "input" as a string which makes batching unclear. PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4895

sam: nice catch. runtime still accepts strings for backcompat but docs should show arrays for batch-first guidance. paste the bad snippet?

lia: current page shows:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1",
  "input": "search term"
}
```
Proposing we replace with:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "open-embed-1",
  "input": ["search term", "second doc text"]
}
```
and a one-line note: "Responses return data as an array that corresponds 1:1 with inputs (stable ordering)."

kevin: agree. two follow-ups: update OpenAPI example under components.schemas.EmbeddingsRequest to use an array, and make sure the code-snippet generator doesn't collapse single-item arrays into a bare string. there's an old template that does that.

docs-bot: lint failure in PR when example used string: components.schemas.EmbeddingsRequest.example.input expected array, found string. CI log: https://ci.redwood-inference/1400/logs/12 :warning:

lia: i've updated the YAML and JS snippet in the PR; also added a short migration note explaining SDKs will auto-wrap single-string inputs but recommend explicit arrays for bulk indexing. added a Python example showing `if isinstance(payload['input'], str): payload['input'] = [payload['input']]`.

sam: please also include a response example showing `data` is an array with index fields. support gets confused.

lia: added response example and pushed. running CI.

docs-bot: CI passed on branch fix/embeds-examples (build 498) :white_check_mark: https://ci.redwood-inference/1400/builds/498

kevin: merged. follow-up: file an SDK issue to ensure generators across languages emit arrays for `input`. i'll create the ticket.

sam: thanks all 389 closing thread.
